title: Swahili Roasted Cassava
community: Zanzibar street vendors and coastal markets
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Muhogo wa Kuchoma — cassava peeled and roasted over charcoal until the exterior is lightly charred and the interior is soft, creamy, and slightly smoky. Eaten with chilli and lime — the simplest and most honest Tanzanian street food.
longDesc: Roasted cassava is the most honest street food in Tanzania — the cassava vendor, the charcoal jiko, the cassava roasting until the exterior chars. Eaten with chilli salt and lime, it is the most direct expression of East African food culture.
ingredients: 1 large cassava root — peeled and cut into sections
steps: Peel cassava and cut into 10cm sections.
Roast over charcoal coals 25—30 minutes, turning regularly.
The exterior should be lightly charred in places; interior creamy when pierced.
chefTips: Medium coals — slow roasting produces the creamy interior.
Test with a skewer — no resistance means done.
commonMistakes: Too high heat — exterior burns before interior cooks.
cookingScience: The cassava starch gelatinises during roasting — converting from raw starch granules to a soft, digestible gel. The charring on the exterior adds pyrazines — the aromatic compounds responsible for the roasted, slightly smoky flavour.
sustainabilityTips: Cassava is Tanzania's most climate-resilient staple.
culturalNote: Roasted cassava is the street food that needs no introduction — the vendor, the smoke, the charred cassava and the lime. It is Tanzania in its most honest and direct form.
